claim: For every integer \(k\ge1\), let \(\Sigma_k=\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}\) and \(L_k=\{a_i a_i:1\le i\le k\}\). The minimum number of states of an epsilon-free NFA recognizing \(L_k\) whose underlying simple transition graph is a bipartite cactus is exactly \(k+1+\lceil k/2\rceil\), whereas the unrestricted epsilon-free NFA minimum is \(k+2\).
scientific_limitations: The exact formula applies to \(L_k=\{a_i a_i:1\le i\le k\}\) over \(k\) distinct symbols and epsilon-free NFAs.
The lower bound uses the cactus condition; the matching construction is bipartite. No result is claimed for arbitrary finite languages or epsilon-NFAs.
title: Exact cactus-NFA state complexity for a diagonal finite language
